title: Alcohol or other substances used to cope
summary: For plans that are not substance-use plans, when the client uses alcohol or other substances to manage mood, anxiety, trauma reminders or sleep. Every item records substance use, so any export that includes one carries the 42 CFR Part 2 notice.

problems.label: Using alcohol or other substances to manage feelings or sleep

definitions.text: Drinks or uses other substances to calm down, numb feelings, shut out memories or get to sleep, on several days a week.
Notices that use goes up when mood, anxiety or sleep gets worse, and that mood or anxiety is often worse the next day.
Has mixed feelings about cutting down and has not yet looked at the pattern with the clinician.

longTermGoals.text: The client understands how substance use and their main difficulties feed each other, chooses a personal goal for use, and has other ways of coping that work for them.

shortTermObjectives.text: At intake and at each plan review, the clinician asks about alcohol and other substance use with a brief validated screen and talks through the results with the client. The answers are not entered into this tool.

Before any plan to stop or sharply cut down, the clinician checks for risk of dangerous withdrawal (for example daily heavy drinking, regular sedative use, or past seizures or severe withdrawal) and arranges a medical review when it is present.
By week 3, map at least 3 recent times of use: the feeling or situation just before, what the substance did in the short term, and what happened afterwards, to see what the use does for the client.
By session 4, the client chooses a goal for use in their own words (for example stopping, cutting down to set limits, or not using to get to sleep), with reasons that matter to them.

Over weeks 3 to 10, use at least 2 substance-free ways of coping (for example urge surfing, a grounding skill, a call to a support person or the sleep routine) during at least 3 urges a week, and note what happened.

If use does not change or is causing harm, discuss by week 8 integrated treatment for both concerns or a referral to substance-use care, including medication options and mutual-help groups, and agree on next steps.

collaborativeNote: Ask about substance use in a matter-of-fact, non-judgmental way and let the client choose the goal. Check for withdrawal risk before any plan to stop. Record only what the plan needs; no amounts, dates or other details are entered in this tool. 42 CFR Part 2 prohibits unauthorized use or disclosure of these records. Do not add names or other identifying details. Resource only. Not a substitute for clinical judgment.
